title: Lying over for an injective integral ring map
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] (every element of $S$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\varphi(R)$). Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$; that is, the map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, is surjective.

mathlib_searches.query: lying over: injective integral ring extension, every prime ideal of R is the comap of a prime ideal of S
If R ⊆ S is an integral extension then Spec S → Spec R is surjective (lying over theorem)
